title: Consent
purpose: Find the recorded consent of a coded participant in a study.
summary: The recorded consent of each coded participant in each study.

tasks.title: Find a participant's consent
steps: Type the participant code in [[Participant]] or [[Search]] and select [[Apply]].
Select the row to open the consent.

good_to_know: Participants are coded identifiers only. The system holds no names.
Status comes from the newest record and any withdrawal in effect.
Do not contact is Yes after any withdrawal.

sections.title: Tabs
paragraphs: Consents lists one row per participant and study; Withdrawals lists the withdrawals recorded on consent pages.

items.label: Consent
items.description: Participant code and study code, e.g. P-000123 · DEMO-STUDY; opens the consent.

items.label: Status
items.description: Consented, Refused or Withdrawn, from the newest record and any withdrawal in effect.

items.label: Form
items.description: The form version of the current record.

items.label: Expires
items.description: The current record's expiry date, or No end date.

items.label: Do not contact
items.description: Yes after a withdrawal of contact or any withdrawal.

items.label: Participant
items.description: A coded participant identifier, matched exactly (capitals not required). The specimen record links here filtered to its participant.

items.label: More filters: Do not contact
items.description: Only consents flagged Do not contact.

items.label: Search, filters, Apply, Clear all
items.description: Search and the filters narrow the rows on the server; Apply runs them and Clear all removes every filter and the search. Active filters show as chips you can remove one by one. An invalid filter shows an error and no rows rather than everything.

items.label: Columns
items.description: Shows or hides columns for you; the first column stays.

items.label: Sorting and paging
items.description: Click a sortable heading to sort; click again to reverse. Rows per page: 25, 50 or 100. The count under the table is the number of rows matching the filters.

items.label: Export CSV
items.description: Downloads all matching rows across pages as UTF-8 CSV, using the current filters and sort. If more than 10,000 rows match when the export runs, the download stops. Narrow the filters and try again. Text that starts like a spreadsheet formula gets a leading apostrophe. The audit trail records who downloaded the selection, the filters and the number of data rows in the file. With no matches, the CSV contains only the header and the audit count is zero.

sections.title: Actions and access
paragraphs: Every staff role (admin, manager, technician, viewer) can open this page. Only admin and manager see and can use the buttons that change records; the server refuses the change to anyone else.
Record consent (admin and manager) opens the consent form. Participants are coded identifiers only; the system holds no names.
